title: AI data-centre boom puts India’s power grid under pressure, drives up upgrade costs
key_facts: At a July meeting of the North Eastern Regional Power Committee, Power Grid Corporation of India said the estimated cost of upgrading the control and energy-management systems (SCADA/EMS) at the region's load despatch centres rose from Rs 521 crore to about Rs 688 crore because AI-driven demand was making the hardware more expensive.

An Odisha representative at an Eastern Regional Power Committee meeting last December flagged a 'ramping impact' when industries such as data centres buy power in bulk; slow-ramping generators could face penalties.

The Central Electricity Authority's National Power Committee noted in February that data centres 'typically exhibit high constant loads, with possible ramping characteristics'; Grid-India is studying their demand patterns, media reports suggest.

The Northern Regional Load Despatch Centre warned in February that data centres could switch rapidly to backup power, creating a 'credible risk of abrupt load rejection'; Noida has 125 MW of operational data-centre capacity with over four times that in the pipeline.
A grid incident on 12 June in the western region shed about 32 MW of data-centre load.

Alok Kumar of the All-India Discoms Association said extra data-centre demand of one to two gigawatts a year 'will not make a huge difference' and will be concentrated in a few cities, but state transmission utilities would have to upgrade quickly, which could be hard in urban areas.

Kumar said data-centre operators must bear the cost of extending transmission to their facilities and that it should not be passed on to all consumers of the same distribution company, citing CERC rules.
quote_evidence: The reason: AI-driven demand was making hardware used in supervisory systems more expensive.

“An incremental demand from data centres ranging between one and two gigawatts per year will not make a huge difference,” he said, adding that “[moreover], this would be concentrated in certain cities only, like in Hyderabad, Mumbai, Chennai, Visakhapatnam and the Delhi NCR region, among others.”
why_it_matters_hint: Grid officials across India are planning for data-centre load and its costs.
event_date: 10 Oct 2026 (article); meetings between Dec 2025 and Jul 2026
notes: The Hindu is a subscriber piece but the full text was in the page. Based on committee minutes and documents the paper reviewed; one quoted industry voice.
